What the study asks:
Here, we used 23 years of observations on co-flowering synchrony among 142 animal pollinated plant species in three common dryland ecosystems of the southwest USA to address, (1) Which climate variables best predict co-flowering synchrony, and are climate predictors generalizable across ecosystem types? We then paired flowering phenology with 18 years of co-located monthly abundance data for 88 bee species to evaluate, (2) Does the seasonal stability of bees track co-flowering synchrony independent of climate, and does this relationship differ between specialists and generalists? Finally, we used long-term trends to ask, (3) Has synchrony changed over time and consistently among ecosystems?

Qs addressed in this script:
Q2 does the seasonal stability of bees track synchrony, independent of climate, and how does this differ between specialists and generalists?

## Analysis 3: Co-flowering overlap & Bee Stability 
### Prepare data
```{r}
#change to your working dir
setwd("~/Documents/co-flowering synchrony/Updated 10:23:26")

# import full 2002 - 2019 bee abundance data 
bee.2019<-read.csv("data/SEVBeeData2002-2019_revised2023-07-19.csv",stringsAsFactors = T) 

# turn complete sampling month and complete sampling year into factors
bee.2019$complete_sampling_month <- as.factor(bee.2019$complete_sampling_month)
bee.2019$complete_sampling_year <- as.factor(bee.2019$complete_sampling_year)

# create unique identifier for each web
bee.2019$web_ID<-as.factor(bee.2019$transect)

# remove start/end date columns and collapse by month
bee.2019 <- bee.2019 %>% dplyr:: select (-c("start_date", "end_date", "direction", "color")) %>% 
  dplyr:: group_by(year, month, web_ID, ecosystem, complete_sampling_year) %>%  
  dplyr:: summarise(across(where(is.integer), sum))


# import tallied bee data (includes new data from 2020-2021 and some pre-2020 stragglers)
bee.tally<- read.csv("data/bee_tally.csv") %>% 
  separate(col = web_ID,
           into = c("web_ID", "direction"),
           sep = 2) %>%
  separate(col = web_ID,
           into = c("ecosystem", "web"),
           sep = 1, remove = FALSE) %>% 
  filter(!ecosystem %in% c("J", "P"))
         
# make wide 
bee.tally.wide <- bee.tally %>%  pivot_wider(
  id_cols = c(year, month, web_ID, ecosystem),
  names_from = code,
  values_from = abundance,
  values_fn = sum,
  values_fill = 0)

# merge tallied data with larger data set 
bee <- bind_rows(bee.2019, bee.tally.wide) %>%
  dplyr:: group_by(year, month, web_ID, ecosystem) %>%  
  dplyr:: summarise(across(where(is.integer), sum),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(across(5:360, ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
summary(bee)

# calculate total bee abundance
bee$abundance<-rowSums(bee[,5:360])
summary(bee$abundance)

# calculate richness, diversity, evenness
bee$richness<-specnumber(bee[,5:360])
bee$shannonH<-diversity(bee[,5:360])
bee$evenness<-bee$shannonH/log(bee$richness)

# import phenological synchrony
async<-read.csv("data/plant_overlap_climate_filtered.csv",stringsAsFactors = T) 

# create unique identifier for each web
async$web_ID<-as.factor(paste(async$site,async$web,sep=""))
bee$web_ID <- as.factor(bee$web_ID)
# check that they match
  summary(bee$web_ID) 
  summary(async$web_ID)

# remove 2016/2017 (partial sampling years)
bee<- bee %>% filter(!year %in% c("2016", "2017"))

# import M. Kazenel LH trait data
bee.spec <- read.csv("data/lhtraits_2023-08-29_forpub.csv")
#remove bees with unknown or parasitic diet breadth
bee.spec<- bee.spec %>% filter(diet_breadth != "unknown") %>%  filter(diet_breadth != "parasitic") %>% 
# some of the species have question marks  
filter(diet_breadth != "polylectic?") %>% filter(diet_breadth != "oligolectic?") 
sort(unique(bee.spec$diet_breadth))

# counts for number of gen vs specialist and total
bee.spec %>% 
  count(diet_breadth, sort = TRUE)
# out of 341 species: 86 specialists, 81 generalists 

```

### Calculating Bee Stability - POPULATION  
This represents population-level stability, calculating individual stability values for each species.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# Bee stability over each species' ACTIVE WINDOW + whole season
# Rare species excluded (< 10 non-zero records). Window = one global, contiguous
# min-max non-zero month per bee species (across all years/ecosystems/transects);
# stability = 1 / CV of monthly abundance over those active window months each year.
# ============================================================================

bee_long <- bee %>%
  dplyr:: select(-c(abundance, richness, shannonH, evenness)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, ecosystem, web_ID, month),
               names_to = "species", values_to = "sp_abundance") %>%
  inner_join(bee.spec %>% dplyr:: select(code, diet_breadth), by = c("species" = "code"))

# Exclude truly rare species: keep those with >= 10 non-zero species x month records
keep_species <- bee_long %>%
  filter(sp_abundance > 0) %>%
  count(species, name = "n_rec") %>%
  filter(n_rec >= 10) %>%
  pull(species)
bee_long <- bee_long %>% filter(species %in% keep_species)

# One global, contiguous active window (min & max non-zero month) per species
sp_window <- bee_long %>%
  filter(sp_abundance > 0) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(min_mo = min(month), max_mo = max(month), .groups = "drop")

bee_wide <- bee_long %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(year, ecosystem, species, web_ID, diet_breadth),
              names_from = month, values_from = sp_abundance,
              values_fn = sum, values_fill = 0) %>%
  left_join(sp_window, by = "species")

month_cols <- as.character(sort(unique(bee_long$month)))
M  <- as.matrix(bee_wide[, month_cols]); storage.mode(M) <- "numeric"
mm <- as.integer(month_cols)

# stability = 1 / CV ; NA when < 2 months or zero total (CV undefined)
inv_cv <- function(v) {
  if (length(v) < 2 || sum(v) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  m <- mean(v); s <- sd(v)
  if (m == 0 || s == 0) return(NA_real_)
  1 / (s / m)
}

# MAIN: stability over each species' active window
bee_wide$bee.stability.win <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(bee_wide)), function(i) {
  inwin <- mm >= bee_wide$min_mo[i] & mm <= bee_wide$max_mo[i]
  inv_cv(M[i, inwin])
}, numeric(1))

# SUPPLEMENT: stability over the whole sampled season (all months)
bee_wide$bee.stability.full <- apply(M, 1, inv_cv)

# Average species-level stability to diet breadth per transect x year
agg_stability <- function(col) {
  bee_wide %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) %>%
    group_by(year, ecosystem, web_ID, diet_breadth) %>%
    summarise(bee.stability.sp = mean(.data[[col]]),
              bee.stability.se = sd(.data[[col]]) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(diet_breadth = as.factor(diet_breadth))
}
bee_cast_sp   <- agg_stability("bee.stability.win")   # MAIN  (active window)
bee_cast_full <- agg_stability("bee.stability.full")  # SUPPLEMENT (whole season)

# ---- Species counts by site and diet breadth (species retained after rarity filter) ----
# bee_long holds zeros for every site, so filter to records where the species was caught
sp_counts_site <- bee_long %>%
  filter(sp_abundance > 0) %>%
  distinct(ecosystem, species, diet_breadth) %>%
  count(ecosystem, diet_breadth) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = diet_breadth, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(-ecosystem)),
         ecosystem = dplyr::recode(ecosystem, B = "Plains grassland",
                                   G = "Desert grassland", C = "Desert shrubland"))
sp_counts_site
#roughly the same proportions based on site and same diversity

# overall (each species counted once)
bee_long %>%
  filter(sp_abundance > 0) %>%
  distinct(species, diet_breadth) %>%
  count(diet_breadth)
# 40 specialists and 48 generalists after filtering for acitivty window
```

### 3.1 Bee stability over time (two-stage)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Bee stability over time -- two-stage (transect = unit of replication),
# parallel to the synchrony-over-time analysis in 02, with diet breadth added.
# ============================================================
bee_time <- bee_cast_sp %>%
  dplyr::filter(web_ID != "C3") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ecosystem_type = factor(dplyr::recode(ecosystem, B = "Plains grassland",
                            G = "Desert grassland", C = "Desert shrubland"),
                            levels = c("Plains grassland","Desert grassland","Desert shrubland")),
    diet_breadth = factor(diet_breadth))

# keep transect x diet series with >= 5 years for a reliable Stage-1 slope
ty_n    <- bee_time %>% dplyr::distinct(web_ID, diet_breadth, year) %>%
  dplyr::count(web_ID, diet_breadth, name = "n_years")
keep_td <- dplyr::filter(ty_n, n_years >= 5)
bee_time_s <- bee_time %>%
  dplyr::semi_join(keep_td, by = c("web_ID","diet_breadth")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year_scaled = as.numeric(scale(year)))

# Stage 1: one temporal slope per transect x diet
bee_slopes_year <- bee_time_s %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ecosystem_type, web_ID, diet_breadth) %>%
  do(tidy(lm(bee.stability.sp ~ year_scaled, data = .))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(term == "year_scaled") %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(estimate), std.error > 0)

gen_ty  <- subset(bee_slopes_year, diet_breadth == "polylectic")   # generalists
spec_ty <- subset(bee_slopes_year, diet_breadth == "oligolectic")  # specialists

# Stage 2a: global temporal trend per diet (intercept-only = t-test of mean slope vs 0)
summary(lm(estimate ~ 1, data = gen_ty))
summary(lm(estimate ~ 1, data = spec_ty))

# Stage 2b: ecosystem contrast (per diet) and diet-breadth contrast
anova(lm(estimate ~ ecosystem_type, data = gen_ty))
anova(lm(estimate ~ ecosystem_type, data = spec_ty))
anova(lm(estimate ~ diet_breadth,   data = bee_slopes_year))

# ---- 1/SE-weighted robustness (matches synchrony over-time) ----
summary(lm(estimate ~ 1, weights = 1/std.error, data = gen_ty))
summary(lm(estimate ~ 1, weights = 1/std.error, data = spec_ty))
anova(lm(estimate ~ diet_breadth, weights = 1/std.error, data = bee_slopes_year))
#bee stability not changing over time by any rate, and weighting by the variance of the slopes does not change this
```

### 3.2 Bee stability ~ synchrony models, and evaluating whether climate alters their relationship
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Q3 bee-stability models —
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))   # Type III w/ interactions

bc <- bee_cast_sp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(web_ID = as.character(web_ID)) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(async %>% dplyr::mutate(web_ID = as.character(web_ID)),
                    by = c("year", "web_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(web_ID != "C3") %>%         
  dplyr::mutate(web_id       = factor(web_ID),
                year_fact    = factor(year),
                diet_breadth = factor(diet_breadth))

rich_ty   <- read.csv("data/richness_by_transectyear.csv")
bc <- bc %>% dplyr::left_join(rich_ty, by = c("year","site","web"))
summary(bc$n_species)                  


# base model: synchrony * diet
bee_syn    <- lmer(bee.stability.sp ~ mean_overlap * diet_breadth * site +
                      (1 | web_id), REML = FALSE, data = bc)
anova(bee_syn, type = 3) 
   
## COOL-SEASON (SPRING) PRECIP ######
bee_syn_clim <- lmer(bee.stability.sp ~ mean_overlap * diet_breadth * site 
                     + season.precip.spring + (1 | web_id), REML = FALSE, data = bc)
anova(bee_syn_clim, type = 3)

#Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
#                                 Sum Sq  Mean Sq NumDF DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
#mean_overlap                   0.037576 0.037576     1   394 11.7868 0.0006598 ***
#diet_breadth                   0.084498 0.084498     1   394 26.5049 4.159e-07 ***
#site                           0.025736 0.012868     2   394  4.0364 0.0183962 *  
#season.precip.spring           0.020500 0.020500     1   394  6.4304 0.0116039 *  
#mean_overlap:diet_breadth      0.002883 0.002883     1   394  0.9042 0.3422423    
#mean_overlap:site              0.010869 0.005435     2   394  1.7047 0.1831586    
#diet_breadth:site              0.001299 0.000649     2   394  0.2037 0.8158034    
#mean_overlap:diet_breadth:site 0.001593 0.000797     2   394  0.2499 0.7790293 

AICc(bee_syn, bee_syn_clim)
#in this case, the climate model wins by dAICc of 4. Adding climate, while it significantly predicts stability, adds information to make this a better fitting model to the data, and makes synchrony a stronger predictor

MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(bee_syn)      # synchrony * diet only
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(bee_syn_clim)   # + cool-season precip
#adding climate only raises R2m from 0.35 to 0.36, basically no gain in explanatory power

qqnorm(resid(bee_syn)); qqline(resid(bee_syn)); hist(resid(bee_syn))

## PDO ######
bee_syn_clim1 <- lmer(bee.stability.sp ~ mean_overlap * diet_breadth * site + annual.PDO +
                       (1 | web_id), REML = FALSE,
                     data = bc)
anova(bee_syn_clim1, type = 3) 

AICc(bee_syn, bee_syn_clim1, bee_syn_clim)
#adding PDO does not improve model fit- dAICc of 3. No difference, we retain simpler model.

MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(bee_syn)      # synchrony * diet only
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(bee_syn_clim1)  # + PDO
#this does not change R2m at all, so no added explanatory power

#based on this, we retain that synchrony predicts seasonal bee abundance stability, while there may be independent climate-stability relationships, this is seperate from and does not add explanatory power or negate our stability~synchrony model. 
```

###Inference from best model
```{r}
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

# ---- Selected model, refit simpler model under REML for inference ----
bee_syn_clim <- lmer(bee.stability.sp ~ mean_overlap * diet_breadth + site + season.precip.spring +
                       (1 | web_id), data = bc, REML = TRUE)

# 1. Fixed-effect slopes (estimate, SE, df, t, p) — Satterthwaite via lmerTest
summary(bee_syn_clim)$coefficients

# 3. Overall synchrony slope (averaged over diet, precip at mean)
emtrends(bee_syn_clim, ~ 1, var = "mean_overlap")
#stability declines by 0.07 with 95% CI of (0.11-0.03) for 1 unit increase in synchrony

diff(range(bc$mean_overlap, na.rm = TRUE)) * -0.07
-0.05684636 / mean(bc$bee.stability.sp, na.rm = TRUE) * 100 
#across the observed range of synchrony, from 0.19-1, 
# stability declines by about 10% relative to the stability mean

# 4. Per-guild synchrony slopes + the interaction contrast
emtrends(bee_syn_clim, ~ diet_breadth, var = "mean_overlap")      
pairs(emtrends(bee_syn_clim, ~ diet_breadth, var = "mean_overlap")) # generalist vs specialist
# diet_breadth mean_overlap.trend     SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
# oligolectic             -0.0515 0.0285 381   -0.107  0.00449
# polylectic              -0.0878 0.0285 381   -0.144 -0.03184
#not sig difference but only polylectic (generalists) CI does not cross zero, stronger slope overall

# 5. Precip slope (already in the coef table, but as a trend for clarity)
emtrends(bee_syn_clim, ~ 1, var = "season.precip.spring")

# 6. Diet-guild stability means (the dominant effect), synchrony & precip at their means
emmeans(bee_syn_clim, ~ diet_breadth)
#diet_breadth emmean      SE   df lower.CL upper.CL
# oligolectic   0.524 0.00414 37.2    0.515    0.532
# polylectic    0.600 0.00414 37.2    0.591    0.608
```

### 3.5 Figure: bee stability vs co-flowering synchrony
```{r}
bc$diet_label <- factor(ifelse(bc$diet_breadth == "polylectic", "Generalist", "Specialist"),
                        levels = c("Generalist", "Specialist"))
bc$site <- factor(bc$site, levels = c("B", "G", "C"))
site_labels <- c("B" = "Plains\ngrassland", "G" = "Desert\ngrassland", "C" = "Desert\nshrubland")

# ---- Refit the selected model
bee_syn_clim <- lmer(bee.stability.sp ~ mean_overlap * diet_breadth + season.precip.spring +
                       (1 | web_id), data = bc, REML = TRUE)

# ---- Model-predicted synchrony slope (pooled over diet, precip at mean) ----
ov_grid <- seq(min(bc$mean_overlap, na.rm = TRUE),
               max(bc$mean_overlap, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)

pred_stab <- as.data.frame(emmeans(bee_syn_clim, ~ mean_overlap,
                                    at = list(mean_overlap = ov_grid)))

# ---- (A) Stability vs synchrony ----
stab_syn_plot <- ggplot(pred_stab, aes(x = mean_overlap, y = emmean)) +
  geom_point(data = bc, aes(x = mean_overlap, y = bee.stability.sp, color = site),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.18, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3, color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = ms_site_colors, labels = site_labels, name = "Site") +
  labs(x = "Co-flowering synchrony", y = "Seasonal bee stability (1/CV)") +
  ms_theme

stab_syn_plot
ggsave("figures/FIGURE3_stability_synchrony_site_diet.svg", stab_syn_plot, width = 15, height = 6.5)
ggsave("figures/FIGURE3_stability_synchrony_site_diet.png", stab_syn_plot, width = 15, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
```
